newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela fuel truckers ask for gov't protection.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela fuel truckers ask for gov't protection.

text.p: Venezuela's fuel transport union Fevetraph said Tuesday it feared losing out in the government's plan to liberalise the domestic fuel market and called for state protection.
Fevetraph represents 1,600 truckers in Venezuela which transport 89 percent of the 48 million litres of gasoline and diesel delivered in the country every day.

"Fevetraph believes that we need to save the national commercial heritage... with a law stopping the anti-democratic concentration of a few efficient economic agents," Fevetraph chairman Gilberto Tovar said in a statement to reporters.
He called for the new internal market law currently going through Congress to include preferential treatment for existing transporters.
State fuels retailer Deltaven, which was set up recently to compete in the new open market, was reviewing its fuel transport policy without consulting Fevetraph, he added.
The government wants to see the domestic market opened to competition by the end of this year, with a year transition period during which prices will rise to world levels.
Tovar said Fevetraph had asked Congress to extend this grace period to the trucking business.
His members were also worried by a "proliferation" of road tolls which are currently paid by the government, but would pass to the truckers under the new rules.

Tovar said the average age of Fevetraph road tankers was 20 years and that it needed $670 million dollars to renew 40 percent over five years. Current state-administered tariffs of 2.4 bolivars (0.5 cents) per litre covered only maintenance, he added.
